title: VA Home Loan Guaranty Partial Claim Ceiling Percentage on Loans with an Earlier Partial Claim
content:
The ceiling percentage for a VA partial claim on a VA Home Loan Guaranty loan depends on whether a partial claim has already been paid on the same loan and, if so, how long before today the latest one was paid, as the partial claim entries in the loan's money transactions show.

## Ceiling percentage

| Partial claims on the loan | Latest partial claim paid | Ceiling percentage of the unpaid principal balance |
|---|---|---|
| At least one already paid | Less than 24 months before today | The recent-repeat ceiling, 15 percent |
| At least one already paid | At least 24 months before today | The older-repeat ceiling, 25 percent |
| None paid | — | The program's partial claim ceiling, 30 percent on every program |

The repeat window is 24 months; a latest partial claim paid exactly 24 months before today falls on the older-repeat row.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical loans)

| Months since the latest partial claim on the loan | Ceiling percentage |
|---|---|
| 3 | 15 |
| 23 | 15 |
| 24 | 25 |
| 60 | 25 |
| No earlier partial claim | 30 |

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

On an unpaid principal balance of 200,000.00 dollars at the first unpaid installment, with a latest earlier partial claim paid 10 months before today, the ceiling percentage is 15, so the ceiling is 200,000.00 multiplied by 15 and divided by one hundred, or 30,000.00 dollars.
